transcript:
Header: 2026-03-28 14:00 PT | Duration 46m | Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Mark (Lumenica), Priya (Lumenica SRE), Ethan (CTO)

[00:00] Sofia: alright everyone, uh thanks for joining. today is the weekly pilot sync, and we wanted to run through the canary node incident from last friday, the fallback routing behavior, and next steps for the kernel rollback test. Daniel has the slides and a quick timeline.

[00:22] Daniel: cool, yeah i pulled the packet captures and the metric graphs. quick TLDR — at ~10:14am your canary node saw a sharp egress drop, p50 latency spiked from 68 to around 420 ms, and the automatic fallback routed ~14% of traffic to the regional fallback. the fallback path handled requests but there was higher tail latency.

[00:45] Mark: yeah and just to add — we also saw retries from our app tier, so user-facing errors for about two minutes. the firewall logs show a handful of denied flows to the edge cluster, that might be related.

[01:10] Priya: to be clear, the denied flows were to the redwood-private control plane ip, but only for the canary host, not the whole cluster. i'm guessing some egress NAT mapping changed after the kernel update we applied last week.

[01:34] Daniel: right so our hypothesis is a kernel-level MTU/conntrack difference that caused asymmetric routing for some TCP handshakes, leading to intermittent resets. hence fallback triggered. when that happened the KV cache warm paths weren't hitting as expected which increased per-token overhead.

[01:58] Ethan: mm, okay. is that consistent with the metrics you published in the shared sheet? i saw a big jump in the CPU tokenization metric, that seems odd.

[02:16] Sofia: link to the sheet's in the chat — https://redwood.app/pilot/metrics — the CPU bump is likely due to increased decode retries, so more cycles per request. daniel, you wanna show the timeline slide?

[02:34] Daniel: yep. so timeline: 10:12 kernel package applied to canary host, 10:14 first spike, 10:16 fallback started, 10:18 automatic scaled up a fallback pool, 10:20 retries peaked, 10:22 slow recovery once we forced a drain and reprovisioned the node.

[03:05] Mark: question — how deterministic is the fallback decision? like, does it kick in on p95 thresholds or on 5xxs? we've seen it sometimes route too aggressively and it increases cross-region cost.

[03:28] Daniel: fallback policy is heuristic-based — by default it watches request error rate and latency windows. you can tune aggressiveness; currently it's set to favor availability which means it may route early. we can lower sensitivity to reduce cross-region routing but then your user-experienced errors window could grow.

[03:55] Priya: can we get a mode that prefers local degraded path instead of cross-region? we have strict data residency concerns and egress costs are high.

[04:10] Sofia: yes — we have a region-first policy you can enable, it was off for this pilot by default. i'll enable a test flag for the canary to prefer local degraded instances before cross-region fallback and we'll validate.

[04:30] Ethan: also, the kernel rollback — what's the risk? are we talking about service interruption?

[04:42] Daniel: low risk if done carefully. we recommend a single-host dry-run outside peak, with autoscale disabled and a pre-approved rollback checklist. if conntrack tables are cleared there may be transient resets for connections on that host only.

[05:05] Mark: okay, schedule window? our prime hours are 9 to 5 eastern, so anything after 22:00 PT is fine for us.

[05:15] Sofia: noted. we'll target next tuesday evening PT. action items — daniel will draft the rollback checklist, mark will share the firewall egress snippets and traceroutes, sofia will update the fallback playbook and enable region-first test flag.

[05:40] Priya: quick nit — the telemetry on the private control plane seemed delayed by ~30s during the incident. is that on our end or your agent?

[05:52] Daniel: likely a combination — our agent batches heartbeats under high load to avoid stampeding, and your network dropped a few heartbeats. we'll push a diagnostic build that increases heartbeat frequency for that dry-run so we can get better granularity.

[06:14] Mark: can you put that diag build in a feature branch? our infra team wants to run it in a non-prod canary.

[06:25] Daniel: will do, i'll post the branch link in the follow-up.

[06:40] Ethan: competitors — just for context, our procurement asked about Anthropic and Bedrock as alternatives. chief concern is single-vendor dependency and predictability of fallback behavior.

[06:58] Sofia: understood. we highlighted runbook and observability improvements in the last deck and we'll include the rollback dry-run results in the contract discussion.

[07:15] Mark: one more ask — can you produce a short postmortem note for last week's canary incident? we need it for our internal compliance review.

[07:28] Sofia: yes, we'll draft a 1-page postmortem including timeline, root cause hypothesis, mitigations, and action items. expect that in 48 hours.

[07:40] Priya: and please include the exact traceroute samples and the firewall rule lines — those are the things our security team will want to see.

[07:52] Daniel: i'll attach the packet captures and traceroute logs. note: some hostnames in the capture were anonymized by the transcription, we'll include raw files.

[08:10] Sofia: wrap-up: who owns what — daniel: kernel checklist & diag build (due 2026-04-06); mark: firewall rules + traceroutes (due 2026-03-30); sofia: fallback playbook + pricing note + postmortem (due 2026-04-02). we'll reconvene after the dry-run.

[08:35] Ethan: sounds good. any objections to the next sync tuesday same time?

[08:42] Sofia: works for us, i'll send calendar invite. thanks everyone.

[08:50] (meeting ends)

Notes: occasional transcription mis-hearings present — e.g., "KV cash" in auto-transcript; redwood product names sometimes as "Redwood Privat". Shared artifacts referenced: pilot metrics sheet, rollback checklist draft, playbook link.
